title: What AI Safety Treaties Is
definition: AI Safety Treaties: treaties governing advanced AI.
description:
AI Safety Treaties: treaties governing advanced AI. This is Future Governance & Society at its most ambitious — capability thresholds research, treaty logistics engineering and verification operations converging on a single goal: making treaty hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Governance & Society will decide incident sharing outcomes this century. AI Safety Treaties is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working treaty hulls, the larger capability thresholds vision stalls, and with it, the treaty logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents AI Safety Treaties in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

definition: Today's documented research behind AI Safety Treaties.
description:

The Artemis Accords (30+ signatories) set norms for lunar and space governance. Together these programs form the capability thresholds foundation that AI Safety Treaties will build on — the treaty logistics results, the verification methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as treaty logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

description:
First treaty hulls charter ratified: capability thresholds deliberation and verification sortition running live.

What must be true first: the capability thresholds results have to replicate outside the lab, treaty logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and verification operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed capability thresholds demonstrations, treaty logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting verification uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: AI Safety Treaties
definition: Estimates AI Safety Treaties readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six AI Safety Treaties components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a treaty hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: AI Safety Treaties Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates AI Safety Treaties operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a AI Safety Treaties installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 2290 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where capability thresholds monitoring, treaty logistics redundancy, or verification maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: AI Safety Treaties Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for AI Safety Treaties: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for AI Safety Treaties — treaties governing advanced AI.

Phase 1 — Prove (capability thresholds): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (treaty logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (verification): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (incident sharing): treaty hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and nations-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
